title: Overtime: what the adopted budget set aside and what was paid
question: Which departments pay much more overtime than their adopted budget provides, year after year?
finding: From fiscal 2019 to 2026 the adopted budgets set aside $1.83 billion for overtime and the ledger records $2.79 billion paid; paid overtime exceeded the budget in 8 of 8 years. Police paid 2.12 times its overtime budget over the eight years and the Sheriff 1.83 times; 6 of the 12 departments with at least $1 million a year of overtime budget went over in every year.
how: Object "Overtime" (character Salaries), all funds, adopted budget (xdgd-c79v) against the Controller's ledger (bpnb-jwfb), fiscal 2019 to 2026. Departments with an average overtime budget of at least $1 million a year.
limits: The budget is the original appropriation; supplemental appropriations and transfers made during the year are not in it. Departments often budget less overtime than they expect and pay for it from salaries left unspent by vacancies, so overtime above budget is not money spent without authority. Police permanent salaries ran under budget in every year; the Sheriff's savings on permanent salaries were smaller than its overtime overrun.
